newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament amends banks guarantee fund law.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament amends banks guarantee fund law.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament amended a law on the banking guarantee fund (BFG) by giving it access to more information on ailing banks and increased its guarantees for individual savers' deposits.

Deputies voted 308 to four with 109 abstentions to approve the new regualtions, which will enforce better cooperation among the BFG and administrators of bankrupt banks, but also increase the contributions to the fund paid by banks.
"The new bill makes many regulations and definitions much more precise, hence we will face much less obstacles in our work," BFG president Ewa Kawecka told Reuters.

Under the new law banks will pay to the fund 0.4 percent of their balance-sheet assets and guarantees as well as 0.2 percent of off-balance sheet committments and contingent claims. Under the old law banks only had to pay 0.4 percent of their risk-weighted assets.
The fund was created in 1995 to take over guarantees of bank deposits from the state treasury and to help ailing banks restore financial liquidity.
The amendments increase guarantees for individual savers' deposits to the equivalent of 4,000 Ecus from the current 3,000 Ecus.

They also oblige the central bank to contribute 30 percent of interest generated on banks' obligatory reserves it holds to the fund, to improve the BFG's funding. So far all the interest from obligatory reserves went an agriculture fund.
The bill now needs to clear the sentate, which has a month to scrutinise it, and be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski to become law.
